uae.unit: EUR bn (USD converted at ECB annual averages as in trade_full.json); 2026 = January-August, not annualised
uae.basis: UAE customs (FCSC) basis: goods recorded at the UAE border with Russia as partner. Total of to_rus + from_rus matches the Ministry of Economy / Foreign Trade 'non-oil trade' totals (USD 10.8bn 2022, ~11.0bn 2023, 11.5bn 2024, 20.4bn 2025), which equal the customs totals including the small HS 27 imports.

consistency.reexports_json: reexports_to_RUS central in reexports.json (EUR 2.27/3.90/3.19/3.97/2.65 for 2022-2026) is kept for 2022-2024 (3.19 vs 3.19 here); for 2025 and 2026 the re-export part of the larger export total is EUR 4.78 (3.54-6.11) and 3.27 (2.15-4.39). Raise reexports_to_RUS 2025 to 4.78 and 2026 to 3.27 and move the extra to origins with the same origin_shares; the UAE keeps the margin as now.
consistency.reexports_from_rus: The extra 2024-2026 gold and stones are mostly passed on (UAE passes on 84-91% of its direct Russian gold; refine.json first buyers HKG 30%, IND 19%, CHE 15%, TUR 14%). reexports_from_RUS should rise to about EUR 5.3 (2024), 9.8 (2025) and 4.3 (2026 Jan-Aug) central, so the UAE's own net payments rise much less than its imports.
consistency.crea_fuel: CREA fuel delivered to the UAE (EUR 0.8/5.6/6.1/2.1/1.6/0.2 for 2021-2026) is the total; the part already in UAE customs is fuel_from_rus_in_uae_customs (EUR 0.08/0.27/1.07/0.37/0.62/0.26). The fuel addition from audit2 Q2 must be CREA minus that customs part, floored at zero: EUR 0.73/5.35/4.98/1.77/0.98/0.00. For 2024-2026 audit2 assumed no customs fuel, so the addition falls by 0.37/0.62/0.19.
consistency.hidden_gold: Keep hidden UAE gold at zero for 2022-2026: the gold is now inside the trade layer (Swissaid 66 t for 2024; 2025-2026 estimated).
consistency.armenia_route: Armenian-routed Russian gold collapsed in 2025 (Armenian exports -36%, precious-metal re-exports to the UAE down ~60%); the 2025 rise in direct UAE gold is largely that route moving back to direct shipments. Armenia's 2025-2026 imports of Russian gold in the map should be checked against this (not done here).

sources.name: UN Comtrade (UAE FCSC reports): UAE imports from Russia 2021-2023 by HS (TOTAL, 27, 71, 7102, 7108), exports (X) and re-exports (RX) to Russia
UAE Ministry of Foreign Trade press release (Zawya): non-oil trade with Russia USD 20.4bn in 2025, +77.7% on 2024, nearly double the 2022 level of USD 10.8bn
Finance Middle East: UAE-Russia non-oil trade about USD 11.5bn in 2024 (+5% on 2023); H1 2025 +75%
Gulf Today / UAE Ministry of Economy: 2022 imports from Russia AED 30.1bn, re-exports AED 9bn, national exports AED 1bn; gold AED 20bn, diamonds AED 6.1bn
UAE embassy in Moscow (MOFA): bilateral trade about USD 12bn in 2025 (Russian-side measure), Russian exports led by petroleum products, gold and precious metals
TASS via InvestFuture: Russia-UAE turnover record USD 10.2bn in 2023; USD 8.9bn Jan-Sep 2025 (Alikhanov, Russian side)
Swissaid: United Arab Emirates more than ever a hub for conflict gold (UAE-reported 2024: 66 t / USD 5.4bn of gold from Russia, 78 t from Armenia)
Reuters (via mining.com): 75.7 t of Russian gold to the UAE Feb 2022-Mar 2023 in Russian customs records; 96.4 t in 2022 in Comtrade
Interfax: Hong Kong imports of Russian gold 92.1 t (USD 10.5bn) in 2025, mainland China USD 3.3bn
ARKA / World Bank: Armenia's 2025 exports -36% on a sharp fall of gold and diamond re-exports, mainly to the UAE
CREA Russia Fossil Tracker (fuel delivered to the UAE, as used in audit2 Q2)

uae.reasoning: The official USD 20.4bn is UAE customs trade with Russia; the map's EUR ~11bn (USD ~12bn) for 2025 rests on an IMF IMTS import estimate (USD 8.1bn) and an export value carried forward from 2023, so it misses about USD 8bn. 2021-2023 are the UAE's own FCSC records in Comtrade, which reproduce the Ministry totals exactly (2022: 8.19 + 2.59 = 10.78 vs 10.8). 2024 is pinned by the Ministry total (USD 11.5bn) and Swissaid's 66 t of Russian gold (USD 5.4bn); exports stay near the trade_full estimate. For 2025 the USD 8.9bn rise is split with three anchors: gold prices rose ~44%; the Armenian gold route collapsed, so Russian gold that went UAE-via-Armenia in 2024 (78 t) went more directly; and the Russian-side turnover (USD 8.9bn Jan-Sep, about 12bn for the year, which appears to leave out gold) implies non-gold trade of USD 10-12bn including Russian fuel that UAE customs miss, i.e. UAE exports to Russia of roughly USD 5-7bn. Gold therefore takes USD 8-12.5bn (73-114 t, against Russia's exportable 220-260 t after Hong Kong's 92 t and China's 25 t). 2026 Jan-Aug: Russian gold moved to Hong Kong (99.7 t by July), so UAE gold falls to an estimated 15-52 t; exports run at the 2025 rate. Ranges on the split are wide; the yearly totals for 2022-2025 are tight.

refugees.unit: EUR bn per year, gross public cost to the host government (2026 = January-August)
refugees.eu_funded_note: eu_funded is the part of the host's cost paid from EU funds: CARE/FAST-CARE re-use of 2014-2020 cohesion funds, the EUR 3.4bn REACT-EU pre-financing (April 2022), AMIF/BMVI emergency aid and reallocations, ESF. It is EU-budget money. If the map counts EU-level spending on refugees inside EU aid (spread over members by budget share), subtract eu_funded from the host's cost; if it does not (the Kiel EU-institutions line covers aid to Ukraine, not refugee costs inside the EU), keep the host's gross cost and do nothing. Estimates are given where a national source names the EU share; elsewhere eu_funded is null (unknown, likely small).

residual_allocation.correction_to_premise: Belarus's pro-rata share of the residual is EUR 1.7/2.0/2.1/3.2bn for 2022-2025 (EUR 9.0bn in total, not a year), plus 2.1 for Jan-Aug 2026. In the current site/data.json it IS added to Belarus's sales to Russia on top of the official Belstat/Union State totals (from_rus 23.9/25.1/26.4/27.1/18.9 vs official 22.2/23.1/24.3/23.9/16.8); the audit2 finding that it vanished predates commit 72ff61c.

own_exports_missed_by_partner_data.why: The map uses Belarus's own official totals (Union State 2022, Belstat/NBRB and Russian-side totals 2023-2026), not partner mirror data, so nothing is missed because Belarus stopped publishing by partner. High allows for classified military-industrial deliveries; Russia's FCS also leaves out such goods, so they are unlikely to sit in the FCS gap.

eaeu_transit_unrecorded.why: Mirror test as for Kyrgyzstan: partners' reported exports to Belarus excluding Russia (USD 15.1bn 2021, 12.8bn 2022, 18.1bn 2023, 16.6bn 2024; +5% CIF) against Belarus's non-Russian goods imports (NBRB total FOB imports less official imports from Russia: 16.1, 14.9, 18.6, 20.2bn). No growing gap: Belarus records at least what partners say they sent, so goods do not cross Belarus to Russia unrecorded at scale.

valuation_basis.why: Belarus-basis totals run 3-5% above Russian-basis totals (2022 Union State scaled by 1.03-1.05; 2025 Belarusian side ~USD 54.9bn vs Russian side 50.9-51.9bn). Russia's FCS imports therefore contain less from Belarus than the partner sum, so Belarus's own contribution to the FCS-minus-partners gap is negative.

recorded_reexports_in_official_exports.why: Not part of the residual, but the same question: Belarus's official exports to Russia include goods it imported (China's exports to Belarus rose from USD 2.7bn in 2021 to 5.8/6.6/7.2bn in 2023-2025: cars, electronics, machinery; Turkey's and, in 2023, Poland's and Lithuania's rose too). Taking 45% (35-60%) of China's increase and 30% of the others' as passed on to Russia. These should be moved from Belarus to the origin countries like other hubs (Belarus keeps a 3-15% margin).

release_to_other_countries.why: Belarus's current share plus the valuation offset (central): the gap that really belongs to others. Re-spread it with the residual rule (pro rata to reported sales, coalition weight 0.25), i.e. mostly China, Kazakhstan, Turkey; or recompute the residual with Belarus's official exports in the partner sum (trade_full's Belarus split, EUR 23.8bn in 2022, was 1.6bn above the official 22.2bn, so the residual itself was understated by that amount).

belarus_from_rus_change_central.why: Remove the pro-rata residual (1.72/2.0/2.1/3.2/2.13) and move the recorded re-exports net of a 7% margin (0.28/1.60/1.68/1.80/1.32) to origins.

reexport_share.definition: Share of the crude refined in Belarus (Russian crude plus 1.6-1.9 Mt of domestic crude) that leaves the country as oil products, by mass; the same share applies to Russian crude imports
reexport_share.note: After 2022 almost no importer records Belarusian oil products (partners' imports from Belarus of HS 2710: USD 0.87bn in 2022, of which Ukraine 0.76bn in Jan-Feb; 0.10bn 2023; 0.15bn 2024). The cargoes loaded at Ust-Luga and St Petersburg are booked as Russian origin by buyers and by CREA, so buyers' payments 'to Russia' for these products partly reach Belarus (processing margin) and only the crude value reaches Russia.

belarus.reasoning: (a) Belarus enters the partner sum with its own official totals, so its pro-rata share of the residual (EUR 9.0bn over 2022-2025) has no basis: partner data miss nothing for Belarus, a mirror test shows no unrecorded transit, and Belarus-basis figures are 3-5% above what Russia books, which makes Belarus's own part of the gap slightly negative. Set Belarus's residual to zero (range -1.2 to +1.0 a year) and release EUR 2.5-4.1bn a year to the other countries; separately move the re-exports recorded inside Belarus's official exports (mainly Chinese goods, EUR 0.3-1.9bn a year) to their origins. Effect on Belarus's headline 2022-2026: -27.6% to -22.2% of GDP. (b) About 22-26% of Belarus's imports from Russia are crude for Mozyr and Naftan and 10-11% gas; roughly half of the crude refined leaves as products (61% in 2019, 47% in 2022, 52-53% since). Before the war the products went to the UK, Ukraine and the Netherlands; since 2022 they go through Russian ports to third countries under Russian origin, and increasingly to Russia itself (22% in 2025, about a third in 2026).

LBN.fix: Use a baseline without the 2019 fuel spike: mean of 2018, 2020 and 2021 imports from Russia (EUR 0.48bn, range 0.42-0.55) instead of the 2019-2021 mean (0.66). 2019 imports (USD 1.34bn, of which fuel 1.19bn) were inflated by subsidised fuel bought for smuggling into Syria before the 2019-2020 collapse; Lebanon's fuel imports were 4.3 (2018), 6.5 (2019), 3.2 (2020), 3.9 (2021) USD bn. Keep sales and services baselines (both tiny).

services_eur_bn.2018_note: no partner breakdown published for 2018; the 2019-2021 level (EUR ~0.02bn each way) is the best estimate

MRT.fix: Count Russian sellers, not Russian-origin labels. Pre-war 'imports from Russia' in Mauritanian customs (USD 0.126/0.123/0.031bn of fuel in 2019-2021) were traders' cargoes declared by origin; Russia recorded only USD 1-2m of fuel and USD 16-36m of all goods to Mauritania. Set the to_rus baseline to Russia's own export records x1.1 (EUR 0.021bn, 0.013-0.035) and treat the origin-labelled cargoes as Russian oil bought via other countries, before and after the war, with its own pre-war level (EUR 0.065bn). Fish exports to Russia (USD 0.16/0.095/0.051bn, HS 0303) did stop in 2022; Russia itself recorded only USD 1.5-1.9m of fish imports from Mauritania, so most was catch by Russian-operated trawlers sold on elsewhere: keep, but the profit share is all Mauritania lost.

LCA.fix: Saint Lucia's 'imports from Russia' are one Russian mirror record of USD 0.285bn of crude (HS 2709) in 2021 to the Cul de Sac storage and transshipment terminal, carried forward to 2022-2025 by the growth rule. Saint Lucia's own reports show zero imports from Russia in 2019-2020. Set to_rus (years and baseline) and the derived war-time price extra to zero; label it a transit terminal.

BES.fix: Bonaire's imports from Russia are a 2019 Russian mirror record of USD 0.064bn of fuel oil (HS 2710) to the BOPEC storage terminal, extended by estimates. Terminal storage and bunkering are transit, not use on an island of 25,000 people. Set to_rus and its price extra to zero (or keep only a bunker share at the low end).

BWA.fix: Botswana's pre-war imports from Russia were rough diamonds (HS 7102: USD 0.143/0.111/0.173bn in 2019-2021) bought for sorting and resale; they stopped with the G7 diamond sanctions. Botswana did not use them; treat it like a gold hub: pass the stones on to their buyers (or drop the flow) and keep a trading margin of 5% (2-10%) as Botswana's own baseline.

SYC.fix: Shipping income is booked to the Seychelles because shadow-tanker managers are incorporated there; these are fronts for Russian (Sovcomflot chain), Emirati and Indian operators. Apply the UAE foreign-share scaling from refine.json (keep 20%, 5-50%) and give the rest to the Russian-controlled pool; the Seychelles keeps only company and registry fees.

MLT.fix: Malta's services bought from Russia drop from EUR 0.133bn (2022) to 0.003bn (2023-2025), a 98% fall in one year that reflects confidential cells reported as zero, and the COVID-rebound multiplier (1.35) is applied to services that are not travel. Treat 2023-2026 as missing (2022 level falling with EU services imports from Russia: 0.08/0.07/0.06/0.04) and use no rebound for non-travel services.
